ecologyNotes:
Mycorrhizal with oaks and other hardwoods. Cap 1.5–6 cm, brown overall at first, developing yellow undertones and becoming yellowish brown to yellowish with a brown spot over the disc — considerably duller than the large golden chanterelles a beginner expects, so anyone using colour as the primary character is using the wrong one. Undersurface has well-developed, closely spaced false gills running down the stem, yellow throughout development, often developing cross-veins with maturity. Stem fairly slender, equal or tapering downward. Flesh whitish to yellowish, unchanging when sliced. Odor fragrant, reminiscent of apricots. Grows alone, gregariously, or in small clusters. Summer.
